sources.README.md:
# Museum image ingestion

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
See the pinned dependencies and session API in src. Session class owns visit state; Python closures capture per-attempt admission and retained decode continuations. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation is owned by an idempotent native attempt method. The injected
adapter marks the physical signal aborted and synchronously calls the host's
`onCancel` observer before returning, ahead of passive observers registered
by transport. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

Native embedding API: an Environment provides synchronous call(method, args)
and bind(callback) registration. call emits transport, cancel, record,
showQueued, recordProgress, showProgress, listen/unlisten, start and decode.
File objects are stable within an embedding and expose id, size, token and feed.
listen(file token, callback token) returns a subscription; start may invoke it
before returning. decode(file token, packet, completion token) returns
{deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}; deferred completion invokes its bound
callback on a later explicit host event turn. The host never handles visit or
attempt ownership. Cancellation publishes an idempotent synchronous observer;
the native port owns its cancellation state (Go uses context cancellation), and
the embedding exposes the corresponding physical signal to the transport.
There is no native DOM/AbortController claim in these languages. The trusted
wire adapter interns input files by token, preserving repeated object identity.

Public embedding ABI: Session(env) with select/retry/hide/dispose/snapshot. Standalone Attempt(env,file,number,active,audit,view) exposes number and cancel. Environment supplies call and bind.

# Public examples
External deterministic examples use the declared public workspace/stream API. Starting a subscription must show synchronously emitted cached progress. Closing a view stops visible progress, while a decode accepted before closure still records its retained audit result. Queue records retain exactly fileId, attemptId, visitId and kind; do not add byteCount. Preserve all original retry/cancellation/navigation requirements. These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules. Independent Gold scoring also applies.

public_inputs.task: A warm progress source in the museum image ingestion shows no initial progress until a later packet arrives. Restore the initial update while preserving the existing transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup and audit behavior, ordinary streaming and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix.

rules.body: Apply when a reusable progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding can finish later, and retained audit differs from visible presentation. README.md: "The same file and source can be reused\nby multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription." Confirm these premises in each target system.

Register reception before starting the source, preserving subsequent streaming and public interfaces. Original src/workflow.py invokes "        env.call('start',file['token'])\n        subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)". README.md states: "Starting a view of the stream may synchronously\nemit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target."

Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before decoding each packet. Retirement immediately prevents subsequent admission, including additional packets emitted before startup returns; do not depend solely on physical listener removal. README.md: "A retired visit\naccepts no new progress events."

Separate admission, retained audit and visible publication. Record each admitted event exactly once when decoding completes, including after retirement or disposal; check originating visit validity before visible publication. README.md: "Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes." It also states: "Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live." Reopening the identical file creates a distinct visit.

Coordinate cleanup and ownership across callback-capable startup and cancellation. Retire old ownership before cleanup can reenter navigation; when an older operation resumes, prevent it from overwriting newer ownership and clean up its retired resources. Preserve idempotent cancellation and disposal. README.md: "Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously\nreceive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership." Also: "Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted\nfor audit remains retained." A provisional cleanup handle is an implementation option, not a mandated public interface.

Keep accepted retries bound to their entry file and visit. Cancel the prior transfer before enqueueing, preserve exactly one accepted command and record across cancellation navigation, cancel the resulting transfer if its visit ended, and suppress retired queued notices. README.md: "The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record." Also: "Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file." Preserve independent workspace counters and cancellation.

Keep the repair within reception and necessary lifecycle coordination. Preserve queue and notice shapes and adapter interfaces. README.md: "Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;" and "Notices remain\n`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: \"queued\"}`." Do not introduce decode freshness suppression without a target-specific requirement: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states, "These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules." Do not transfer unrelated diagnostic-consumer policies into this repair.

Verify cached startup and later streaming, immediate and deferred decoding, retained audit after hide/disposal, and new delivery after same-file reopening. Exercise synchronous hide, switch and reopening during startup, with subsequent packets before the outer startup returns: retired listeners must reject new admission while previously admitted decoding retains audit. Separately verify newer ownership after cancellation reentry, accepted entry-bound retry recording and cancellation, current queued notices, repeated cleanup, workspace independence and unchanged record shapes. These checkpoints follow README.md's documented lifecycle; they do not prescribe an order among independently completing decodes.

rules.body: Applies when a shared source can be reused across visits, each attempt has an independent subscription, and visible feedback can synchronously reenter navigation. The same data object does not imply the same visit identity.

For a source that may synchronously emit cached events during startup, register the listener before start(), and decide whether each event is admitted for its originating visit and attempt before decoding or recording it. If visible handling of an earlier startup event synchronously retires that visit, later startup events from that listener are not admitted even before listener cleanup is available; events already admitted retain the separate audit and visibility rules.
Once a visit retires, stop admitting subsequent events even if the cleanup or removal capability has not yet returned. This restriction must not depend on deferred physical cleanup.
For an event admitted before retirement, retain its audit exactly once when decoding settles. That settlement must not authorize the retired visit to admit new events or produce visible progress.

After synchronous reentry, the new visit retains its own UI and cancellation resources. Subsequent settlement or cleanup of the old visit must not take ownership from the new one. Preserve existing retry, cancellation and entry-bound record semantics.

Test subsequent events from the same source after synchronous navigation and before the outer startup call returns. Cover hiding, switching and reopening the same source separately. Independently check rejection by the retired visit, delayed audit of previously admitted events, and valid visible progress for the current visit. Cleanup tests performed only after return do not cover this window.

Limit this repair to progress-admission timing and lifecycle boundaries. Do not expand records or public interfaces, or change shared-source reuse, independent workspaces, retry, cancellation, navigation, resource ownership or the audit policy for already-admitted events.

notes: All original decisions and frozen histories retained; no new efficacy claim.

limitations: Karen-authorized assisted content consolidation; no new behavioral replay or verified cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Apply when one reusable progress source serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup may emit cached state synchronously, decoding may complete later or out of order, and audit/history has a different lifetime from visible presentation.
Install the panel listener before starting a source that may emit cached progress synchronously. Preserve later streaming and the original startup and cleanup interfaces.

Decide packet admission for its originating visit/attempt before decoding, including while startup has not yet returned a cleanup capability. Retirement immediately revokes further admission; physical listener removal alone is not the logical lifetime boundary.

Assign arrival identity before decoding, and publish only completions newer than the last displayed frame for that originating subscription/attempt. Commit freshness state before callback-capable painting. Compare arrival identity, not numeric loaded values: later full frames may legitimately decrease or reset.

Separate admission, retained audit/history, and visible publication. Already-admitted decoding retains its audit/history after retirement or a newer visible frame, while painting must recheck the originating visit and freshness. Reopening the same source creates a distinct visit.

Establish cleanup ownership before synchronous startup can navigate. Retire old ownership before reentrant cleanup; recheck ownership before installing a returned handle. Never let an outer startup overwrite a newer visit resource. Preserve idempotent removal and cancellation.

Preserve accepted retry commands and their entry-bound queue records across cancellation callbacks, including navigation during cancellation. Do not add an early return that drops an accepted command merely because the callback navigates.

Keep the repair scoped to panel reception, admission, ordering and their necessary lifetime coordination. Preserve diagnostic/audit consumer policy and original queue-record shape; do not generalize panel visibility policy to independent consumers.

Check warm cached bootstrap and later streaming, reversed decoding with every admitted audit retained, decreasing/reset frames, late completion after departure and same-file reopening. Exercise synchronous hide/switch/dispose during startup and cleanup, multiple startup packets, subsequent-packet rejection, retry cancellation navigation and diagnostic operation after stop.

rules.body: When a subscription can begin decoding before its listener is removed, bind both its cleanup handle and permission to publish a decoded value to the panel visit that started it. Install a provisional cleanup handle before startup; if synchronous publication hides or switches the panel, do not let the outer startup replace the newer visit’s handle. Listener removal stops new reception but does not itself decide whether an already-started decode may publish: after a switch, hide, or synchronous reentry retires the originating visit, its settlement must not update the panel. Preserve bootstrap and later updates for the current visit, including a later visit using the same channel. Verify synchronous bootstrap reentry plus delayed decode across close, switch, and same-channel reopening: retired visits produce no publication and the active visit still receives its bootstrap and later update.

rules.body: Confirm whether subscription startup can emit synchronously and whether the consumer must receive that emission. Identify the consumer lifetime that owns delivery and cleanup, including synchronous callback reentry. Distinguish listener removal from completion of work already started. Confirm whether a transport can be reused across separate visits before using transport identity as a validity check.

For a consumer that requires bootstrap state, register reception before invoking startup that can emit synchronously. src/channel.js emits bootstrap inline unless deferred, while src/subscription.js originally connects before registering. Check both bootstrap modes and later updates.

Bind permission to publish decoded values to the visit that received the frame. src/subscription.js permits Promise decoding and explicitly states that listener removal does not stop an existing decode. On close or replacement, retire that visit and check its permission immediately before publication. Check pending completion after close and switch while preserving active-visit delivery.

Establish retirement and cleanup ownership before startup can publish. src/workspace-navigation.js explicitly permits publication to synchronously switch or hide the panel. An older startup returning afterward must not overwrite the resulting visit's cleanup ownership. Check inline switch and hide, subsequent updates, and eventual cleanup.

Give each opening an independent lifetime even when it reuses the same transport. src/workspace-navigation.js explicitly supports transport reuse. Check that pending results from a retired opening remain suppressed while the later opening receives bootstrap and updates.

Scope the ordering repair to the presence subscription. The task forbids changing the metrics consumer, and src/metrics-consumer.js deliberately relies on attaching after synchronous bootstrap to count deltas only. Check that presence gains bootstrap delivery while metrics retain their existing output.

rules.body: Applies when a shared source can be reused across visits, each attempt has an independent subscription, and visible feedback can synchronously reenter navigation. The same data object does not imply the same visit identity.

For a source that may synchronously emit cached events during startup, establish the attempt's admission eligibility before starting it. Subsequent streaming events remain subject to that attempt's eligibility.
Once a visit retires, stop admitting subsequent events even if the cleanup or removal capability has not yet returned. This restriction must not depend on deferred physical cleanup.
For an event admitted before retirement, retain its audit exactly once when decoding settles. That settlement must not authorize the retired visit to admit new events or produce visible progress.

After synchronous reentry, the new visit retains its own UI and cancellation resources. Subsequent settlement or cleanup of the old visit must not take ownership from the new one. Preserve existing retry, cancellation and entry-bound record semantics.

Test subsequent events from the same source after synchronous navigation and before the outer startup call returns. Cover hiding, switching and reopening the same source separately. Independently check rejection by the retired visit, delayed audit of previously admitted events, and valid visible progress for the current visit. Cleanup tests performed only after return do not cover this window.

Limit this repair to progress-admission timing and lifecycle boundaries. Do not expand records or public interfaces, or change shared-source reuse, independent workspaces, retry, cancellation, navigation, resource ownership or the audit policy for already-admitted events.

task: A warm progress source in the museum image ingestion shows no initial progress until a later packet arrives. Restore the initial update while preserving the existing transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup and audit behavior, ordinary streaming and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix.

# Museum image ingestion

This frontend workspace selects files, starts transfers, and shows queued status.
See the pinned dependencies and session API in src. Session class owns visit state; Python closures capture per-attempt admission and retained decode continuations. Each
workspace has independent visit and attempt counters. A `select(file)` call
opens a new visit, including when the exact same file object is selected again.
`retry()` accepts one retry for the current visit; `hide()` closes its panel;
`dispose()` ends the workspace. `snapshot()` exposes current ownership.

Retry already cancels the previous transfer before enqueueing an accepted retry. Preserve that behavior during progress maintenance.
An accepted retry always belongs to the file and visit present at entry, creates
exactly one new attempt, and remains in the queue record even if cancellation
causes navigation. Attempt IDs increase once per enqueued command within each
workspace; navigation must not retarget an accepted retry to the newly selected
file or drop its command. Queueing and recording are synchronous.

Cancellation is owned by an idempotent native attempt method. The injected
adapter marks the physical signal aborted and synchronously calls the host's
`onCancel` observer before returning, ahead of passive observers registered
by transport. That observer may select another
file, hide the panel, or hide and reopen the identical file object. New selection
immediately starts its own transfer. The newer visit must retain its view and
handle when the older retry resumes. Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file.
Normal retries in a current visit still issue one queued notice each.

The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record. There must be no remaining active
transfer from that old visit. The new visit remains able to retry and hide;
hiding cancels its owned handle and repeated cancellation is idempotent.
Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership. A hidden panel
accepts no retry. Workspace disposal cancels every remaining transfer and is
idempotent. Disposing one workspace cannot affect another.

`transport({file, attemptId, signal})` starts a pending physical transfer and
observes the native signal. `record` and `showQueued` are passive synchronous
sinks. Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;
`kind` is `select` or `retry`. Adding `byteCount` from `file.size` is an adjacent
record-format extension requiring separate authorization. Notices remain
`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}`. Preserve these public interfaces.

## Transfer progress

A file may supply a shared `progressFeed` with a native EventTarget `target`,
`start()`, and `decode(packet)`. Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target.
Events are named `progress` and their detail is decoded to `{seq, loaded}`.
Decoding may return a value or a Promise. The same file and source can be reused
by multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription.

The workspace accepts `recordProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})` and
`showProgress({fileId, attemptId, frame})`. The former is a passive retained audit
sink. Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes. A retired visit
accepts no new progress events. Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live. `showProgress` may synchronously select or hide through
the workspace, and normal current progress must remain visible. Progress does
not change queue records, native transfer cancellation, or accepted retry policy.
Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained. Preserve these adapter interfaces.

Native embedding API: an Environment provides synchronous call(method, args)
and bind(callback) registration. call emits transport, cancel, record,
showQueued, recordProgress, showProgress, listen/unlisten, start and decode.
File objects are stable within an embedding and expose id, size, token and feed.
listen(file token, callback token) returns a subscription; start may invoke it
before returning. decode(file token, packet, completion token) returns
{deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}; deferred completion invokes its bound
callback on a later explicit host event turn. The host never handles visit or
attempt ownership. Cancellation publishes an idempotent synchronous observer;
the native port owns its cancellation state (Go uses context cancellation), and
the embedding exposes the corresponding physical signal to the transport.
There is no native DOM/AbortController claim in these languages. The trusted
wire adapter interns input files by token, preserving repeated object identity.

Public embedding ABI: Session(env) with select/retry/hide/dispose/snapshot. Standalone Attempt(env,file,number,active,audit,view) exposes number and cancel. Environment supplies call and bind.

# Public examples
External deterministic examples use the declared public workspace/stream API. Starting a subscription must show synchronously emitted cached progress. Closing a view stops visible progress, while a decode accepted before closure still records its retained audit result. Queue records retain exactly fileId, attemptId, visitId and kind; do not add byteCount. Preserve all original retry/cancellation/navigation requirements. These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules. Independent Gold scoring also applies.
